```{r data cleaning}
data2 <- data %>%
  filter(
    age >= 50,
    if_all(c(time, event, age, gender, race, BMI, CHD, TMIMS), ~ !is.na(.)),
    time > 0,
    CHD %in% c("Yes", "No")) %>% 
  ## create mortality time in years
  mutate(time = time/12,
         age_group = cut(age, 
                         breaks = seq(min(age, na.rm = TRUE), max(age, na.rm = TRUE) + 5, by = 10),
                         right = FALSE),
         MIMS_group = cut(TMIMS,
                          breaks = quantile(TMIMS, c(0, 0.333, 0.667, 1)),
                          labels = c("low TMIMS", "medium TMIMS", "high TMIMS"),
                          include.lowest = TRUE))
data2$CHD <- droplevels(data2$CHD)

# define s_grid (length P)
# s_grid <- seq(1/60, 24, length = 1440)
s_grid <- seq(0, 1, len = 1440)

# survival outcome
time <- data2$time
status <- data2$event

# cluster id
cluster_id <- data2$STRAPSU

# functional covariate
X <- data2$MIMS
age <- data2$age

# scalar covariates design matrix Z
# Columns are: (Intercept), age_in_years, bmi
# Z <- model.matrix(~ age + gender + BMI + CHD, data = data2)
Z <- model.matrix(~ gender + BMI + CHD, data = data2)
```

```{r age table}
## Subjects, deaths and censoring rate by 5-year age group in the analysis
## cohort.  Age is top-coded at 80 in NHANES, so the top group is "80+".
age_tab <- data2 |>
  mutate(age_group5 = cut(age, breaks = c(seq(50, 80, 5), Inf), right = FALSE,
                          labels = c(paste(seq(50, 75, 5), seq(54, 79, 5), sep = "-"), "80+"))) |>
  group_by(age_group5) |>
  summarise(n = n(), d = sum(event == 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(age_group5 = as.character(age_group5))
age_tab <- bind_rows(age_tab,
                     tibble(age_group5 = "Total", n = sum(age_tab$n), d = sum(age_tab$d))) |>
  transmute(`Age (years)` = age_group5,
            Subjects = n,
            `Deaths (censoring rate, %)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f)", d, 100 * (1 - d / n)))
knitr::kable(age_tab, align = "lrr",
             caption = "Number of subjects and deaths, with the censoring rate, by 5-year age group.")
```

```{r exploratory analysis}
## Mean MIMS difference (alive - deceased) by time of day x age band.
## Built for two band widths -- 5-year (fig_nhanes.png) and 2-year
## (fig_nhanes_2yr.png).  Age is top-coded at 80 in NHANES, so the top band is
## "80+" in both.  The 2-year bands are noisier: several under age 60 rest on only
## 10-20 deaths.
mims_mat <- unclass(data2$MIMS)
tod_bin  <- ceiling(seq_len(ncol(mims_mat)) / 180)          # 8 windows x 180 min
tod_lab  <- sprintf("%02d-%02d", seq(0, 21, 3), seq(3, 24, 3))
mims_3h  <- sapply(1:8, function(b) rowMeans(mims_mat[, tod_bin == b, drop = FALSE]))
colnames(mims_3h) <- tod_lab

# band:        width of the age bands in years (must divide 30)
# label_every: spacing of the age labels on the y-axis
heat_plot <- function(band, label_every = band) {
  edges <- seq(50, 80, band)
  heat_dat <- as_tibble(mims_3h) |>
    mutate(age_band = cut(data2$age, breaks = c(edges, Inf), right = FALSE),
           status   = if_else(data2$event == 1, "deceased", "alive")) |>
    pivot_longer(all_of(tod_lab), names_to = "tod", values_to = "mims") |>
    group_by(age_band, tod, status) |>
    summarise(mean_mims = mean(mims), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = status, values_from = c(mean_mims, n)) |>
    mutate(diff = mean_mims_alive - mean_mims_deceased,
           tod  = factor(tod, levels = tod_lab))
  stopifnot(nrow(heat_dat) == 8 * length(edges), !anyNA(heat_dat$diff))

  # Tiles sit on numeric axes so the tick labels can mark bin EDGES: 3-hour
  # windows on x, age bands on y.
  heat_dat <- heat_dat |>
    mutate(x = (as.integer(tod) - 1) * 3 + 1.5,
           y = 50 + (as.integer(age_band) - 1) * band + band / 2)
  y_lab <- seq(50, 80, label_every)

  ggplot(heat_dat, aes(x, y, fill = diff)) +
    geom_tile(width = 3, height = band, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                         midpoint = 0,
                         name = "Mean MIMS (alive - deceased)") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 3),
                       labels = c("12 AM", "3 AM", "6 AM", "9 AM", "12 PM",
                                  "3 PM", "6 PM", "9 PM", "12 AM"),
                       expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(y_lab, 80 + band),
                       labels = c(y_lab, ""),   # top band is 80+ (top-coded)
                       expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = "Time of day", y = "Age (years)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          legend.position="bottom",
          plot.margin = margin(5.5, 20, 5.5, 5.5))
}

p_tile     <- heat_plot(band = 5)
p_tile_2yr <- heat_plot(band = 2, label_every = 10)   # every 2-year edge would crowd the axis

ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "fig_nhanes.png"),
       plot = p_tile, width = 5, height = 5, dpi = 500, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "fig_nhanes_2yr.png"),
       plot = p_tile_2yr, width = 5, height = 5, dpi = 500, bg = "white")
```

```{r gibbs sampler}
### run Gibbs sampler
tic()

fit_bayes_int <- gibbs_frailty_interaction(
  time = time,
  status = status,
  cluster_id = cluster_id,
  Z = Z,
  X = X,
  age = age,
  s_grid = s_grid,
  # tuning / priors
  K_s = 15,
  K_age = 10,
  lambda_init = 5000,         
  A_lambda = 1, B_lambda = 0.1, 
  var_gamma = 100,
  A_tau2 = 3, B_tau2 = 2,
  A_sigma2 = 3, B_sigma2 = 2,
  # MCMC
  n_iter = 20000,
  n_burn = 10000,
  n_thin = 1,
  verbose = TRUE
)

time_stamp <- toc(quiet = TRUE)
time <- time_stamp$toc - time_stamp$tic
# saveRDS(fit_bayes_int, file = "fit_bayes_int_k20.rds")
```

```{r frailty histogram}
### Histogram of estimated cluster frailties -- figure for the talk.
### Note: u_hat are posterior MEANS, so they are shrunk toward 0; their spread
### is smaller than tau_hat by design. The gap between the bars and the gold
### curve is that shrinkage, not lack of fit.
library(ggplot2)

u_hat   <- colMeans(fit_bayes_int$u)          # posterior mean frailty per PSU
tau_hat <- sqrt(median(fit_bayes_int$tau2))   # posterior median frailty SD

cat("\n--- frailty summary ---\n")
cat("J (clusters)  :", length(u_hat), "\n")
cat("sd(u_hat)     :", round(sd(u_hat), 3), "\n")
cat("tau_hat       :", round(tau_hat, 3), "\n")
cat("range(u_hat)  :", round(range(u_hat), 3), "\n")
cat("tau^2 95% CrI :", round(quantile(fit_bayes_int$tau2, c(0.025, 0.975)), 3), "\n\n")

p_frailty <- ggplot(data.frame(u = u_hat), aes(x = u)) +

    y = "Density"
```

```{r icc}
### Intraclass correlation of log survival times within a survey PSU.
icc_posterior <- function(fit, var_eps = 1) {
  fit$tau2 / (fit$tau2 + fit$sigma2 * var_eps)
}

icc_draws <- icc_posterior(fit_bayes_int, var_eps = 1)

# Design effect implied by the estimated clustering, at the average PSU size
n_bar      <- mean(table(cluster_id))
deff_draws <- 1 + (n_bar - 1) * icc_draws

qfmt <- function(x, digits = 3) {
  q <- quantile(x, c(0.5, 0.025, 0.975))
  sprintf("%.*f  [%.*f, %.*f]", digits, q[1], digits, q[2], digits, q[3])
}

cat("\n--- clustering summary (log-time scale) ---\n")
cat("median [95% CrI]\n")
cat("tau^2  :", qfmt(fit_bayes_int$tau2),  "\n")
cat("sigma^2:", qfmt(fit_bayes_int$sigma2), "\n")
cat("ICC    :", qfmt(icc_draws),            "\n")
cat("mean PSU size :", round(n_bar, 1), "\n")
cat("design effect :", qfmt(deff_draws, 2), "\n")
cat("P(ICC > 0.01) :", round(mean(icc_draws > 0.01), 3), "\n\n")
```

```{r interaction surface}
reconstruct_interaction_surface <- function(mcmc_out, grid_age = seq(50, 80, by = 1),
                                            grid_s = s_grid, chunk = 2000) {
  require(mgcv)
  sm_tensor <- mcmc_out$meta$sm_tensor

  # 1. Dense evaluation grid; column names must match the te() terms (s_grid, age)
  eval_grid <- expand.grid(s_grid = grid_s, age = grid_age)

  # 2. Tensor basis at the grid.  The sampler builds sm_tensor with
  #    absorb.cons = FALSE, so this is the raw basis -- the same one used to form
  #    the integrated design matrix W.  Hence beta(s, a) = Phi %*% b is exactly the
  #    surface that enters the likelihood.
  Phi_pred <- PredictMat(sm_tensor, eval_grid)

  # 3. Posterior mean: linear in b, so it needs no draws x grid matrix.
  eval_grid$beta_mean <- as.vector(Phi_pred %*% colMeans(mcmc_out$b))

  # 4. Pointwise 95% CrI from the draws, in blocks of grid points.  The full
  #    draws x grid matrix is 10,000 x 44,640 (3.6 GB) for this fit; blocking
  #    caps it at draws x chunk without changing any result.
  eval_grid$lower <- eval_grid$upper <- NA_real_
  for (st in seq(1, nrow(eval_grid), by = chunk)) {
    idx <- st:min(st + chunk - 1, nrow(eval_grid))
    q   <- apply(mcmc_out$b %*% t(Phi_pred[idx, , drop = FALSE]), 2,
                 quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
    eval_grid$lower[idx] <- q[1, ]
    eval_grid$upper[idx] <- q[2, ]
  }

  return(eval_grid)
}

# Get the processed grid
plot_data <- reconstruct_interaction_surface(fit_bayes_int)
# Grid points whose 95% CrI excludes zero (POINTWISE, not a simultaneous band)
plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  mutate(is_significant = case_when(
    lower > 0 ~ 1,
    upper < 0 ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  ))

# Heatmap Visualization
p_beta <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = s_grid, y = age)) +
  # Main Heatmap
  geom_tile(aes(fill = beta_mean)) +
  # Add black contour lines with a mapped aesthetic for the legend
  geom_contour(aes(z = is_significant, color = "Significant (95% CrI)"), 
               breaks = 0.5, 
               linewidth = 0.5) +
  # Define the gradient for the heatmap
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +
  # Define the manual color for the contour legend
  scale_color_manual(name = "", values = c("Significant (95% CrI)" = "black")) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25),
    labels = c('12 AM', '6 AM', '12 PM', '6 PM', '12 AM')
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Time of day (s)",
    y = "Age (years)",
    fill = expression(beta(s, age))
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    # legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.box = "horizontal", # both legends on one line
    # legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "cm"),  # longer colour bar so its tick labels do not collide
    # plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position="bottom"
  ) 

# ggsave("beta_k25_k20.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6)
```

```{r interaction surface}
library(plotly)
library(tidyr)

# 1. Reshape the data into a matrix format
# We need s_grid as columns and age as rows
matrix_data <- plot_data %>%
  select(s_grid, age, beta_mean) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = s_grid, values_from = beta_mean) %>%
  column_to_rownames("age") %>%
  as.matrix()

# 2. Extract axis values
age_axis <- as.numeric(rownames(matrix_data))
s_grid_axis <- as.numeric(colnames(matrix_data))

# 3. Create the 3D surface
plot_ly(x = ~s_grid_axis, y = ~age_axis, z = ~matrix_data) %>%
  add_surface(
    colorscale = list(c(0, "blue"), c(0.5, "white"), c(1, "red")),
    colorbar = list(title = "beta(s, age)")
  ) %>%
  layout(
    title = "K_s = 25, K_age = 20",
    scene = list(
      xaxis = list(title = "Time of Day (s)", ticktext = c('12 AM', '6 AM', '12 PM', '6 PM', '12 AM'), tickvals = seq(0, 1, 0.25)),
      yaxis = list(title = "Age (years)"),
      zaxis = list(title = "Effect Size")
    )
  )
```

```{r predictions}
## Activity tertiles are defined WITHIN each age; the mean activity profile of each
## age x tertile is pooled over gender, CHD and BMI.  The covariates used for
## prediction are fixed separately below (reference subject: male, no CHD, BMI 29).
new_data <- data2 %>%
  filter(age %in% c(50, 60, 70, 80)) %>%
  group_by(age) %>%
  mutate(MIMS_group = cut(TMIMS,
                          breaks = quantile(TMIMS, c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1)),
                          labels = c("low", "medium", "high"),
                          include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(age, MIMS_group) %>%
  summarise(MIMS   = t(colMeans(MIMS)),        # 1 x 1440 mean profile
            n_cell = n(),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(gender = factor("Male", levels = levels(data2$gender)),
         CHD    = factor("No",   levels = levels(data2$CHD)),
         BMI    = 29)

Z_new <- model.matrix(~ gender + BMI + CHD, data = new_data)

times <- seq(0.1, 9, length = 50)             # 10-year horizon; follow-up ends at 9.25 y
pred_surv <- predict_gibbs_interaction(fit = fit_bayes_int, X_new = new_data$MIMS,
                                       age_new = new_data$age, Z_new = Z_new,
                                       cluster_id_new = NULL,   # frailty = 0 for every curve
                                       type = "survival", times = times)
pred_df <- as.data.frame(pred_surv$mean)
colnames(pred_df) <- paste0("t", times)

surv_df <- new_data %>%
  dplyr::select(age, MIMS_group) %>%
  bind_cols(pred_df) %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("t", ignore.case = FALSE),
               names_to = "time", values_to = "survival") %>%
  mutate(time = as.numeric(sub("^t", "", time)),
         age  = factor(age))

p_pred <- ggplot(surv_df, aes(x = time, y = survival, colour = MIMS_group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ age, labeller = labeller(age = function(x) paste("Age:", x))) +
  # Okabe-Ito colours: distinct under red-green colour-blindness
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(low = "#D55E00", medium = "#009E73", high = "#0072B2")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.4, 1), xlim = c(0, 9)) +
  labs(x = "Time in years", y = "Survival probability", colour = "PA level") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  # theme(legend.position            = "inside",
  #       legend.position.inside     = c(0.015, 0.545),
  #       legend.justification.inside = c(0, 0),
  #       legend.background          = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "grey70",
  #                                                 linewidth = 0.3),
  #       legend.key.height          = unit(0.4, "cm"),
  #       legend.title               = element_text(size = 9),
  #       legend.text                = element_text(size = 8))

p_beta_pred <- p_beta + p_pred
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "fig_nhanes_fit.png"),
       plot = p_beta_pred, width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 500, bg = "white")
```

```{r cross validation}
# 1. Initialization
n_folds <- 10

# Ensure tgrid is strictly positive for the Log-Normal AFT (start at 0.1, not 0)
tgrid <- seq(0.1, 8, len = 100) 

# ==========================================
# DEFINE THE TWO FOLD SETTINGS
# ==========================================
set.seed(916)

# --- Setting 1: Split by Cluster (STRAPSU) ---
# All subjects in a given cluster will go to the same fold.
unique_clusters <- unique(data2$STRAPSU)
# Randomly assign each unique cluster to a fold from 1 to 10
cluster_fold_assignments <- sample(rep(1:n_folds, length.out = length(unique_clusters)))
names(cluster_fold_assignments) <- as.character(unique_clusters)
# Map the cluster fold assignments back to the individual rows in data2
fold_setting1 <- unname(cluster_fold_assignments[as.character(data2$STRAPSU)])

# --- Setting 2: Split by Subject, Stratified by Cluster ---
# Subjects are split individually, but cluster proportions are maintained across folds.
# createFolds automatically stratifies when given a factor.
fold_setting2 <- caret::createFolds(as.factor(data2$STRAPSU), k = n_folds, list = FALSE)

# Group the settings into a list to loop through
cv_settings <- list(
  "Setting 1: Split whole dataset by cluster (STRAPSU)" = fold_setting1,
  "Setting 2: Split by individual subjects (Stratified by cluster)" = fold_setting2
)

# ==========================================
# MAIN OUTER LOOP FOR CV SETTINGS
# ==========================================

for (setting_name in names(cv_settings)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n\n********************************************************\n"))
  cat(sprintf("STARTING CROSS-VALIDATION: %s\n", setting_name))
  cat(sprintf("********************************************************\n"))
  
  # Get the fold assignments for the current setting
  fold <- cv_settings[[setting_name]]
  
  # Storage for the Integrated Brier Score (IBS) and C-index for each fold
  IBS_bayes  <- IBS_laft  <- IBS_lfcm  <- IBS_lfcmfr  <- rep(0, n_folds)
  Cidx_bayes <- Cidx_laft <- Cidx_lfcm <- Cidx_lfcmfr <- rep(0, n_folds)
  
  for (i in 1:n_folds) {
    cat(sprintf("\n--- Fold %d / %d ---\n", i, n_folds))
    
    # Split data
    train_idx <- which(fold != i)
    test_idx  <- which(fold == i)
    
    train_data <- data2[train_idx, ]
    test_data  <- data2[test_idx, ]
    
    # ==========================================
    # MODEL 1: Fit & Predict Bayesian lfAFT with frailty
    # ==========================================
    cat("Fitting lfAFT with frailty...\n")
    
    Z_train <- model.matrix(~ age + BMI + gender + CHD, data = train_data)
    X_train <- as.matrix(train_data$MIMS)
      
    Z_test  <- model.matrix(~ age + BMI + gender + CHD, data = test_data)
    X_test  <- as.matrix(test_data$MIMS)
      
    # Safely align columns (handles missing factor levels in the test fold)
    missing_cols <- setdiff(colnames(Z_train), colnames(Z_test))
      
    if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
      for (col in missing_cols) {
        Z_test <- cbind(Z_test, 0)               # Add column of zeros
        colnames(Z_test)[ncol(Z_test)] <- col    # Name it correctly
      }
    }
      
    # Reorder Z_test to perfectly match Z_train and drop any strictly novel levels
    Z_test <- Z_test[, colnames(Z_train), drop = FALSE]
    
    fit_bayes <- gibbs_frailty_interaction( 
      time       = train_data$time, 
      status     = train_data$event, 
      cluster_id = train_data$STRAPSU,
      Z          = Z_train, 
      X          = X_train, 
      age        = train_data$age,
      s_grid     = s_grid,
      K_s        = 10,
      K_age      = 5,
      n_iter     = 20000, 
      n_burn     = 10000,
      verbose    = FALSE 
    )
    
    pred_bayes <- predict_gibbs_interaction(
      fit            = fit_bayes,
      X_new          = X_test,
      Z_new          = Z_test,
      age_new        = test_data$age,
      cluster_id_new = test_data$STRAPSU,
      type           = "survival",
      times          = tgrid
    )
    
    S_bayes <- pred_bayes$mean
    
    # ==========================================
    # MODEL 2: Fit & Predict LFCM with frailty (fcoxFr)
    # ==========================================
    cat("Fitting LFCM with frailty...\n")
    X_train_mat <- matrix(X_train, ncol = 1440, byrow = FALSE)
    X_test_mat <- matrix(X_test, ncol = 1440, byrow = FALSE)
    fit_lfcmfr <- fpcr(time = train_data$time, event = train_data$event, group = train_data$STRAPSU,
                               X = X_train_mat, Z = Z_train[, -1], nb = 10, gp = s_grid)
    
    # Linear predictor for the train set
    pred_lfcmfr_train <- fpcr_predict(object = fit_lfcmfr, time = train_data$time, event = train_data$event,
                                      group = train_data$STRAPSU, X = X_train_mat, Z = Z_train[, -1])
    eta_train <- pred_lfcmfr_train$predictions
    
    # Linear predictor for the test set
    pred_lfcmfr_test <- fpcr_predict(object = fit_lfcmfr, time = test_data$time, event = test_data$event,
                                     group = test_data$STRAPSU, X = X_test_mat, Z = Z_test[, -1])
    eta_test <- pred_lfcmfr_test$predictions
    
    # Survival probability matrix
    S_lfcmfr <- get_breslow_survival(
      eta_train   = eta_train, 
      time_train  = train_data$time, 
      event_train = train_data$event, 
      eta_test    = eta_test, 
      tgrid       = tgrid
    )
    
    # ==========================================
    # MODEL 3: Fit & Predict lfAFT (funAFT)
    # ==========================================
    cat("Fitting lfAFT...\n")
    fit_laft <- fit_lfAFT(data = train_data, y = "time", delta = "event", x = "MIMS", x_as_regex = FALSE,
                          z = c("age", "BMI", "gender", "CHD"),
                          family = "lognormal", k = 10, basis = "cc", s_grid = s_grid, se = FALSE)
    
    S_laft <- predict_lfAFT(fit_laft, test_data, type  = "survival", times = tgrid)
    
    # ==========================================
    # MODEL 4: Fit & Predict LFCM (mgcv)
    # ==========================================
    cat("Fitting LFCM...\n")
    
    N <- nrow(train_data) # number of samples
    # Quadrature weights for Riemann integration
    lvec <- matrix(1 / 1440, 1440, 1)
    # matrix containing quadrature weights for all participants
    L <- kronecker(matrix(1, N, 1),t(lvec))
    # matrix containing functional domain values
    S <- kronecker(matrix(1, N, 1), t(s_grid))
    train_data$S <- I(S)
    #Pointwise product of w i(s) and the quadrature weights, "L"
    train_data$W_L <- I(train_data$MIMS * L)
  
    fit_lfcm <- gam(time ~ age + BMI + gender + CHD + 
                    s(S, by=W_L, bs="cc", k=10), 
                    method="REML", 
                    data=train_data, 
                    weights=train_data$event, # Assuming 'event' is the status indicator
                    family=cox.ph)
    
    N_test <- nrow(test_data) # number of test samples
    # Quadrature weights for Riemann integration
    L_test <- kronecker(matrix(1, N_test, 1),t(lvec))
    # matrix containing functional domain values
    S_test <- kronecker(matrix(1, N_test, 1), t(s_grid))
    test_data$S <- I(S_test)
    #Pointwise product of w i(s) and the quadrature weights, "L"
    test_data$W_L <- I(test_data$MIMS * L_test)
    
    # mgcv::cox.ph evaluates survival probability based on the 'time' column in newdata.
    # We loop over tgrid to build an (N_test x length(tgrid)) survival matrix.
    S_lfcm <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(test_data), ncol = length(tgrid))
    
    for(j in seq_along(tgrid)) {
      tmp_test <- test_data
      tmp_test$time <- tgrid[j] 
      S_lfcm[, j] <- predict(fit_lfcm, newdata = tmp_test, type = "response")
    }
    
    # ==========================================
    # METRICS: Calculate IPCW IBS and IPCW C-Index
    # ==========================================
    cat("Calculating IPCW Brier Scores and IPCW C-Index...\n")
    
    # --- 1. IPCW Integrated Brier Scores ---
    IBS_bayes[i]  <- cal_IPCW_Brier(S_mat = S_bayes, time_test = test_data$time, event_test = test_data$event, 
                                    time_train = train_data$time, event_train = train_data$event, tgrid = tgrid)
    IBS_lfcmfr[i] <- cal_IPCW_Brier(S_mat = S_lfcmfr, time_test = test_data$time, event_test = test_data$event, 
                                    time_train = train_data$time, event_train = train_data$event, tgrid = tgrid)
    IBS_laft[i]   <- cal_IPCW_Brier(S_mat = S_laft, time_test = test_data$time, event_test = test_data$event, 
                                    time_train = train_data$time, event_train = train_data$event, tgrid = tgrid)
    IBS_lfcm[i]   <- cal_IPCW_Brier(S_mat = S_lfcm, time_test = test_data$time, event_test = test_data$event, 
                                    time_train = train_data$time, event_train = train_data$event, tgrid = tgrid)
    
    # --- 2. Extracting Risk Scores ---
    risk_bayes  <- -rowSums(S_bayes)
    risk_lfcmfr <- eta_test
    risk_laft   <- -predict_lfAFT(fit_laft, test_data, type = "link")
    risk_lfcm   <- predict(fit_lfcm, newdata = test_data, type = "link")
    
    # --- 3. Uno's IPCW C-Index Calculation ---
    Surv_train <- Surv(train_data$time, train_data$event)
    Surv_test  <- Surv(test_data$time, test_data$event)
    
    Cidx_bayes[i]  <- UnoC(Surv.rsp = Surv_train, Surv.rsp.new = Surv_test, lpnew = risk_bayes)
    Cidx_lfcmfr[i] <- UnoC(Surv.rsp = Surv_train, Surv.rsp.new = Surv_test, lpnew = risk_lfcmfr)
    Cidx_laft[i]   <- UnoC(Surv.rsp = Surv_train, Surv.rsp.new = Surv_test, lpnew = risk_laft)
    Cidx_lfcm[i]   <- UnoC(Surv.rsp = Surv_train, Surv.rsp.new = Surv_test, lpnew = risk_lfcm)
    
  }
  
  # ==========================================
  # FINAL RESULTS FOR CURRENT SETTING
  # ==========================================
  cat(sprintf("\n=== 10-Fold CV Results for %s (IPCW Integrated Brier Score) ===\n", setting_name))
  cat(sprintf("Mean lfAFT-fr IBS : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(IBS_bayes, na.rm = TRUE), sd(IBS_bayes, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("Mean LFCM-fr IBS  : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(IBS_lfcmfr, na.rm = TRUE), sd(IBS_lfcmfr, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("Mean lfAFT IBS    : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(IBS_laft, na.rm = TRUE), sd(IBS_laft, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("Mean LFCM IBS     : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(IBS_lfcm, na.rm = TRUE), sd(IBS_lfcm, na.rm = TRUE)))
  
  cat(sprintf("\n=== 10-Fold CV Results for %s (Uno's IPCW C-index) ===\n", setting_name))
  cat(sprintf("Mean lfAFT-fr C-idx : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(Cidx_bayes, na.rm = TRUE), sd(Cidx_bayes, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("Mean LFCM-fr C-idx  : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(Cidx_lfcmfr, na.rm = TRUE), sd(Cidx_lfcmfr, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("Mean lfAFT C-idx    : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(Cidx_laft, na.rm = TRUE), sd(Cidx_laft, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("Mean LFCM C-idx     : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(Cidx_lfcm, na.rm = TRUE), sd(Cidx_lfcm, na.rm = TRUE)))
}
```

```{r}
AGE_REF <- 65   # centring value, for numerical stability only

dat_aft <- data2 %>%
  mutate(
    TMIMS_z = as.numeric(scale(TMIMS)),
    age_c   = age - AGE_REF,
    age_grp = cut(age, breaks = c(50, 60, 70, 80, Inf), right = FALSE,
                  labels = c("50-59", "60-69", "70-79", "80+"))
  )

BANDS <- levels(dat_aft$age_grp)

## ---- activity effect within each age band, and overall --------------------
## Bands get a linear age term, the pooled row gets ns(age, 3). The 80+ band is
## skipped automatically: NHANES top-codes age at 80, so age is constant there
## and the term is not identified.
fit_row <- function(dd, lab, age_adj = "none") {
  if (sum(dd$event) < 20) return(NULL)                 # too few events to fit
  rhs   <- "TMIMS_z + gender + BMI + CHD"
  n_age <- length(unique(dd$age_c))
  if (age_adj == "spline" && n_age > 10) rhs <- paste(rhs, "+ ns(age_c, df = 3)")
  if (age_adj == "linear" && n_age >  3) rhs <- paste(rhs, "+ age_c")
  f <- tryCatch(
    survreg(as.formula(paste("Surv(time, event) ~", rhs)),
            data = dd, dist = "lognormal"),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(f)) return(NULL)
  est <- coef(f)[["TMIMS_z"]]
  se  <- sqrt(vcov(f)["TMIMS_z", "TMIMS_z"])
  data.frame(row = lab, n = nrow(dd), events = sum(dd$event),
             ratio = exp(est), lower = exp(est - 1.96 * se),
             upper = exp(est + 1.96 * se))
}

forest_df <- bind_rows(
  lapply(BANDS, function(g)
    fit_row(dat_aft[dat_aft$age_grp == g, , drop = FALSE], g, age_adj = "linear")),
  list(fit_row(dat_aft, "All ages 50+", age_adj = "spline"))
) %>%
  mutate(
    kind  = ifelse(row == "All ages 50+", "overall", "band"),
    label = sprintf("%s\n%s deaths / %s", row,
                    format(events, big.mark = ","), format(n, big.mark = ",")),
    label = factor(label, levels = rev(label))
  )

## same pooled fit with no age term, to size the confounding for the console
naive <- fit_row(dat_aft, "pooled, age-unadjusted", age_adj = "none")

## ---- formal interaction test, flexible age main effect --------------------
fit_int <- survreg(
  Surv(time, event) ~ TMIMS_z + ns(age_c, df = 3) + TMIMS_z:age_c +
                      gender + BMI + CHD,
  data = dat_aft, dist = "lognormal"
)
b_int <- coef(fit_int)[["TMIMS_z:age_c"]]
p_int <- summary(fit_int)$table["TMIMS_z:age_c", "p"]

## ---- console summary ------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n--- exploratory AFT: does the TMIMS effect move with age? ---\n")
cat("Survival-time ratio per +1 SD TMIMS, lognormal AFT,\n")
cat("adjusted for sex, BMI, prevalent CHD and age.\n\n")
print(forest_df %>%
        transmute(row, n, events, ratio = round(ratio, 2),
                  CI = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", lower, upper)),
      row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("\nPooled estimate, age-unadjusted : %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]  <- confounded by age\n",
            naive$ratio, naive$lower, naive$upper))
k <- nrow(forest_df)
cat(sprintf("Pooled estimate, ns(age,3)      : %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]  <- in the figure\n",
            forest_df$ratio[k], forest_df$lower[k], forest_df$upper[k]))
cat("The first sits above every band because older participants are both less\n")
cat("active and closer to death; the bands are age-controlled by construction.\n")

cat(sprintf("\nInteraction (ns(age,3) main effect, linear TMIMS x age):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  %+.5f per year of age, p = %s\n\n",
            b_int, format.pval(p_int, digits = 3, eps = 1e-4)))
if (p_int > 0.05) {
  cat("NOTE: interaction is not significant once the age main effect is\n")
  cat("flexible. Present this figure as 'the effect is substantial at every\n")
  cat("age', not as an age trend.\n\n")
}

## ---- plot -----------------------------------------------------------------
p_age <- ggplot(forest_df, aes(x = ratio, y = label, colour = kind)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1.5, colour = "grey85") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), orientation = "y",
                width = 0.18, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 3.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(band = "#202C64", overall = "#B58500"),
                      guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2, 2.5)) +
  labs(
    x = "Survival-time ratio per +1 SD of total daily activity",
    y = NULL,
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "TMIMS x age interaction p = %s",
      format.pval(p_int, digits = 2, eps = 1e-4)
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(colour = "grey35", size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y        = element_text(colour = "grey20", lineheight = 1.05)
  )
```
